title: Benchmark more open decision models on any hardware
description: Survey (docs/decision-models-survey.md, 2026-09-23) found a dozen open Laya-like System 1 decision models. Goal: measure each one's bias on the same tasks, cues and floors as Jev and Laya, with one engine-adapter pattern (optional pip extras per engine, device auto-detect for MPS, CPU and CUDA, ONNX or GGUF fallback where the model ships one) so the harness runs on any machine with one command. Each child story: adapter in the record's shape, timing on our Mac, predictions written before the first run, every existing cell answered, RESULTS.md column.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Status (2026-09-23): Not started. Open-model coverage work has not begun; the engine-adapter stories under this epic are specced but no runs have happened.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Assessment recorded in BD-eaf72f: strengths are controlled perturbations, explicit comparison floors, preregistration documents, and offline answer-record replay. Priorities are joint uncertainty for excess-over-floor estimates, selection-aware headline reporting, comparable engine coverage with accuracy alongside sensitivity, stimulus validity checks, and bringing staged batch 2 into replay. Assessment covers local commit c18f878, which is behind origin/main; no engines, builds, or tests were run.

right_now_summary: Adapters and the cross-hardware runner are being built, but no benchmark runs have happened yet.
